items.summary: The Janata Dal (Secular) on Monday, August 10, called off its padayatra against the proposed Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township (GBIT) project after police stopped the march near Kaniminike on the outskirts of Bengaluru. The party has now shifted the protest to Freedom Park on August 18, where it plans to hold a larger demonstration under the leadership of JD(S) patriarch and former Prime Minister HD Deve Gowda. The three-day padayatra, led by JD(S) youth wing president Nikhil Kumaraswamy and backed by the BJP, began at Byramangala near Bidadi on August 9. It was scheduled to cover around 38 km before reaching Freedom Park on August 11. On Monday, protesters reached Kaniminike using a service road instead of the Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway. After a lunch break, Nikhil and other leaders attempted to proceed towards the NICE Road junction via Challaghatta Metro station. Police stopped them, citing concerns over traffic congestion. An argument broke out between the protesters and police personnel, and some protesters allegedly pushed police officers and attempted to cross the barricades. items.title: SEBI's Closing Auction Session: Compliance obligations behind a market structure reform
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India's Closing Auction Session ("CAS"), introduced by Circular HO/47/11/11(3)2025-MRD-POD2/I/2765/2026 dated January 16, 2026 ("Circular") and operative since August 3, 2026, replaces the volume-weighted average price methodology that has determined closing prices for equity stocks with active derivative contracts. The Circular has been issued in exercise of SEBI's powers under Section 11(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, read with Regulation 51 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) (Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations) Regulations, 2018, the general statutory basis SEBI relies on to protect investor interests and regulate the securities market through directions to exchanges and clearing corporations. It is worth noting at the outset that CAS is implemented entirely through this circular-and-directions route, not through an amendment to the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations or the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations. items.title: Wildlife department to probe origin of lar gibbon seen in Actor Vikram’s video
items.summary: Actor Chiyaan Vikram has drawn the attention of wildlife authorities and conservationists after sharing a video of himself interacting with a lar gibbon. The species is a threatened primate protected under international wildlife trade regulations. The video, which Vikram posted on social media, showed him playing with a well-grown lar gibbon. It quickly went viral, but also triggered questions over how the exotic animal came to be in a private setting in Chennai and whether its owner possesses the documents required to legally keep it. The lar gibbon, scientifically known as Hylobates lar, is native to Southeast Asia and is listed under Appendix I of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). The species is also classified as a Schedule IV animal under India's amended Wildlife Protection Act. Under CITES, Appendix I covers species facing the highest level of protection and places stringent restrictions on international commercial trade. Possession of an exotic animal in India can also be subject to domestic requirements concerning its acquisition, registration, transfer and supporting documentation. items.title: View that women wearing jeans 'corrupts' boys unacceptable: Delhi HC overturns acquittal in sexual harassment case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently warned that a woman’s choice of clothing cannot be cited to justify sexual harassment against her. Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha made the observation while convicting a man for sexually harassing a 17 year-old-girl. Notably, the judge took critical note that one of the reasons cited for the acquittal was the failure of the police to look into the complaints made by the accused and fifty local residents against the prosecutrix and her mother. Justice Sudha was at a "loss of words" on finding that the alleged “crime” of the sexual assault victim and her mother was living in society without a male member, wearing western clothes, “corrupting” the minds of young boys in the locality, having questionable character and filing false complaints against “innocent boys” of the area. The Court observed that these "complaints" reflected a deeply troubling and unacceptable mindset. “What a girl or woman chooses to wear is a matter of her personal choice.
